score_basis: Non-statistical internal evidence-quality score based on adopted London transport policy, TfL planning guidance and current Active Travel England design resources, with explicit separation of strategic mode-share objectives from scheme-specific trip/access evidence.

sources.label: London Plan 2021 Chapter 10 Transport
sources.fact: Adopted chapter contains Policies T1-T9 covering strategic transport, Healthy Streets, capacity/connectivity, impacts, cycling, parking, servicing and infrastructure funding.

sources.label: London Plan Policy T6 Car parking
sources.fact: Car-free development is the starting point in well-connected locations; elsewhere minimum necessary parking should be provided within maximum standards.

sources.label: London Plan Policy T6.1 Residential parking
sources.fact: Residential parking must stay within maximum standards; at least 20% of spaces require active electric/ultra-low-emission charging with passive provision for the remainder.

sources.label: TfL guidance for planning applicants
sources.fact: TfL states London planning applications should use the Healthy Streets Approach and explains transport-impact assessment expectations.

sources.label: TfL Transport Assessments
sources.fact: TfL provides Transport Assessment guidance/templates; a parcel-level transport effect requires an actual proposal and assessment.

sources.label: TfL trip generation
sources.fact: TfL identifies trip generation as a specific assessment task for estimating new-development trips rather than a value inferred from land area.

sources.label: TfL highway works
sources.fact: TfL notes highway works on London roads are made under Section 278 agreements; a strategic road proximity is not evidence of secured works.

sources.label: TfL freight planning
sources.fact: Applicants are directed to minimise freight impacts; freight/service effects require scheme-specific servicing evidence.

sources.label: Healthy Streets
sources.fact: Mayor/TfL aim for 80% of trips by walking, cycling and public transport by 2041 and at least 20 minutes active travel per Londoner per day.

sources.label: Vision Zero for London
sources.fact: The policy aim is elimination of deaths and serious injuries from London streets by 2041; this is a network safety objective, not a site risk score.

sources.label: Active Travel England Planning for Active Places
sources.fact: ATE is a statutory consultee and its resource brings together existing policy/guidance for walking, wheeling and cycling; it does not supersede NPPF/PPG.

sources.label: Active Travel England site-wide considerations
sources.fact: Site-wide guidance points to movement frameworks, walkable neighbourhoods, Manual for Streets, inclusive mobility and route-quality assessment.

examples.result: 80% sustainable-mode objective retained as London-wide strategy and not assigned to candidate parcels.
Car-free starting point is conditioned on connectivity and proposal context; no automatic parcel parking score.
T6.1 EV charging requirements apply to actual parking provision and do not prove grid capacity.
Trip generation requires an actual development proposal/model; no trip rate is inferred from parcel area.
Section 278 works require agreement/evidence and are not inferred from road adjacency.
Vision Zero is a strategic safety target, not a parcel collision probability.
ATE design resources guide active-place assessment but do not replace statutory policy or site measurements.
No transport promotion occurs without exact site access, current PTAL/connectivity, proposal and impact evidence.
